All seven writes match owned canonical operations and the inspected table/Yoshi/landing consumers. Both rejected document defects are repaired: unnegated animation result versus negated guard is explicit, and accessory report/assert plus subsequent load assignment is documented separately from xC0 overwrite. No compiled assertion or allocation guarantee is asserted.

Completed targeted contradiction checks in ice construction/release/destruction, Popo-hat dispatch, common physics wrappers, aerial collision query and bone mapping. Accept deferrals for named gameplay/article appearance, command producers and callback lifetime, generic destruction scheduling, complete contact semantics, global aerial resets, downstream common-state behavior and compiled section/ABI claims. The fixed TransN2 selector is mapped per fighter kind; it is not a universal numeric joint index. Supported existing names remain descriptive hypotheses. Acceptance covers the seven changes and examined contradictions, not a fresh audit of every inherited retained row.

proposed_facts.reason: Complete owned implementation, actual PpSpecialN callback registrations and both copied-Yoshi consumers establish the mixed-family purpose. TransN2 is a fixed selector mapped to a model-specific bone index, not a universal numeric joint.

Removal is guarded by non-null xC0; both comparison operands are post-call field reads. Only the adjacent explicit-item helper compares against a separately supplied candidate. The replacement-safety correction is supported without assuming destruction scheduling.

The false-query branch contains optional item removal and current-field comparison, followed by Fall regardless of item presence. No old item pointer is saved. Complete ground-contact interpretation remains appropriately deferred.
The literal non-GA_Ground predicate, optional removal, post-call comparison, comma expression, resets and three forwarded arguments match canonical source.

Actual aerial collision registration and the complete body support cleanup and landing-helper dispatch. The value does not promise unconditional destruction, a particular contact interpretation or Hammer-path interruption policy.

The immediate landing consumer has the stated Hammer alternative and otherwise forwards LandingFallSpecial with the unchecked lag division. Neither cited caller nor entry validates positive finite lag.

Exact zero/nonzero guard, direct assignments, motion arguments, callback installation, PEACH resource selection and paired collision reset are present. Positive momentum and complete per-airtime semantics remain explicitly unproved.

contradictions.reason: The archived animation paragraph contradicted itself. The current document repairs it explicitly: an unnegated true frames-remaining result suppresses the local transition; false makes the negated guard true and invokes the respective helper. Neither callback explicitly performs item cleanup.

The omitted accessory ownership boundary is now documented accurately. Existing non-null x20A0_accessory triggers OSReport and HSD_ASSERT; the subsequent source statement assigns HSD_JObjLoadJoint. This differs from the entries' unchecked xC0 overwrite. Compiled assertion outcome and allocation success remain accepted deferrals.

The superseded removal and collision explanations incorrectly generalized saved-old-item protection. The proposed corrections resolve that contradiction: the comparisons read current fields after calls, whereas the explicit-item notification helper genuinely compares candidate identity. Generic destruction scheduling, reentrancy and user-data stability remain deferred.

Guaranteed upward motion, complete per-airtime resets and unconditional special recovery are not established. The proposal correctly preserves unchecked momentum, the literal collision predicate, the Hammer alternative and unchecked lag division. Full contact semantics, global resets and exceptional runtime outcomes remain accepted deferrals.

All five section-subject deferrals are accepted. Visible literals and their source uses cannot establish compiled .sdata2 membership, size, ordering or placement; unchecked momentum also cannot prove positive lift.

Command consumption and immediate item operations are verified, but exact script timing, complete death/damage cleanup and a global single-projectile invariant remain accepted deferrals. Command one can overwrite a tracked reference and is consumed even on failed creation; command two without an item remains pending.

The exclusive copied-Popo scope interpretation conflicts with actual copied-Yoshi consumers and is corrected by the TU purpose. Exact Ice Shot/Egg Lay concept identities, tongue appearance, named phases and no-partner explanations remain deferred for all listed gameplay facts and links. Duplicate relations and historical provenance are not merged or rewritten.

Common-state and physics deferrals are accepted: local animation forwarding and immediate gravity/friction calls do not independently prove fast-fall preservation, complete Wait routing, unconditional descent or terminal bounds for exceptional inputs. Empty IASA bodies prove only callback-local absence of cancellation.

The repaired document's narrow resolution of bone-mapping behavior is independently supported: the callee only reads the per-kind part-to-joint table. Resource validity, article appearance and original-symbol recovery remain deferred; descriptive accessor naming remains supported.

Removal forwards to `Item_8026A8EC`; the destruction callback, when its retained owner is non-null, dispatches native ice to Popo and the alternate kind to Kirby's identity-checking helper, then nulls its retained owner. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/it/kinds/itclimbersice.c#L87-L156 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/it/kinds/itclimbersice.c#L252-L262.\n\n## Reference clearing and ownership caveat\n`ftKb_SpecialNIc_80108CE8` compares the explicit item argument to the current xC0 and writes NULL only on equality. A different item is ignored; NULL against NULL performs a redundant NULL write. This helper does not destroy the item. `ftKb_SpecialNIc_80108D04` does nothing for a null tracked pointer, otherwise requests item removal and reloads fighter user data before its equality test. Crucially, it does not preserve the pre-call item pointer: both sides of its comparison are field reads after the call. With unchanged fighter user data they alias the same field. The same pattern appears in both collision handlers and command-two release. Consequently the baseline's generalized claim that these comparisons protect a newly installed replacement item is not proved and is incorrect as a description of the source. Only the explicit-argument helper has the stated old-item identity guard. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L30-L51, #L132-L169 and #L195-L207.\n\n## Motion callbacks and boundaries\nBoth Anim callbacks do nothing locally while `ftAnim_IsFramesRemaining` is true. On false, the ground callback invokes `ft_8008A2BC`, and the air callback invokes `ftCo_Fall_Enter`. They do not explicitly perform tracked-item cleanup. Both IASA bodies are empty: this establishes no callback-local cancellation, not immunity from damage, death or other engine transitions. Ground Phys unconditionally calls `ft_80084F3C`; air Phys calls `ft_80084EEC`. The ground helper applies common friction, multiplying it only when ABS(gr_vel) is strictly greater than walk_max_vel, then applies ground movement. Equality does not take the multiplier branch; NaN comparisons do not satisfy that ordered greater-than test. The air helper forwards gravity and terminal_velocity to `ftCommon_Fall` and aerial_friction to `ftCommon_ApplyFrictionAir`. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c3617faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L104-L130; canonical revision for this citation is c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3. Helper evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ft_084E.c#L33-L53.\n\nGround Coll branches on `!ft_80082708(gobj)`, optionally removes the tracked item and always invokes Fall on that branch. Air Coll branches exactly on `ft_80081D0C(gobj) != GA_Ground`, optionally removes the tracked item, clears xC4/xC8 and invokes `ftCo_LandingFallSpecial_Enter(gobj, false, specialn_pp_landing_lag)`. The comma expression `(0, fp2->u.kb.xC0)` contributes only its second operand. A GA_Ground result performs no move-specific reset. Do not invert this predicate using the enum spelling: the query updates collision positions and returns GA_Air for a successful underlying collision result unless another helper suppresses it. The full low-level ground-contact meaning remains unresolved. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L132-L169 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ft_081B.c#L105-L123.\n\nThe landing consumer has an optional HammerLanding branch. Otherwise it enters LandingFallSpecial with allow_interrupt=false and playback rate `(0.1F + fp->x2EC) / landing_lag`. Neither this TU nor that entry guards zero, negative, NaN or infinite lag. Exceptional values therefore are not sanitized into a guaranteed positive finite duration. Likewise velocity and spawn attributes are assigned or used arithmetically without finite-value checks; a negative or NaN vertical-momentum attribute cannot be documented as a guaranteed upward boost. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftCommon/ftCo_Landing.c#L103-L113.\n\n## Trailing copied-Yoshi accessor and interface conventions\n`ftKb_SpecialNYs_80109238` returns `ftParts_GetBoneIndex(GET_FIGHTER(gobj), FtPart_TransN2)` as Fighter_Part, without local validation or writes. The copied-Yoshi item setup consumes it as the owner attachment selector; teardown uses it in an owner-joint lookup before sampling position, then optionally clears destroy_type and clears its victim references. This cross-file use explains why the TU boundary is broader than its filename. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L211-L214 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/it/kinds/itkirbyyoshispecialn.c#L28-L75.\n\nAll owned r3 parameter subjects correspond to the first game-object argument; the sole r4 subject is the explicit Item_GObj* candidate in the notification helper. The empty IASA functions do not dereference their parameters. The removal definition spells HSD_GObj*, whereas the owned header spells Fighter_GObj*; source-level role is clearly fighter user data, but ABI/register and typedef equivalence were not independently compiled here. PAD_STACK is a matching convention, not gameplay behavior. The rendered aliases ItemIceCheckOwn, ItemIceRemove, Enter, SpecialAirNIc_Enter and SpecialNYs_GetBoneIndex are plausible descriptive hypotheses, not recovered canonical symbols. The renderer reported no parse errors; it substitutes function names only, including foreign aliases whose meanings must not be treated as evidence.\n\n## Unproved layout and integration assumptions\nNo compiled object or section artifact was supplied. The literals 0.0F, 1.0F and -10.0F are visible, but neither a 12-byte .sdata2 layout nor their exact section placement follows from that fact. Kirby's copied-Popo neutral-special entry routines, eight ground/air motion callbacks, a shared command-driven ice-item accessory callback, and two tracked-item cleanup helpers. Its final function, ftKb_SpecialNYs_80109238, belongs to the copied-Yoshi family rather than the copied-Popo family. The filename therefore does not describe an exclusive boundary. The active motion table actually registers the eight PpSpecialN callbacks, with ground and air entries sharing FtMoveId_KbSpecialNPp; this is stronger evidence than interpreting numeric motion identifiers. Popo-hat cleanup dispatch calls ftKb_SpecialNIc_80108D04. Its central corrections are valid: current-field comparisons are not saved-old-item identity checks; the PEACH resource index must not be silently changed; the aerial collision predicate must not be inverted based on enum spelling; source literals do not establish .sdata2 layout. This review additionally avoids retaining an entire baseline fact merely by narrowing its meaning in the disposition reason. Facts containing unverified gameplay, timing, or article-identity assertions remain unresolved even where their core local operations are supported.\n\n## Entry routines and resources\nftKb_SpecialNIc_80108D64 clears throw_flags, cmd_vars[0], and u.kb.xC0; calls Fighter_ChangeMotionState for ftKb_MS_PpSpecialN with 0, 0.0F, 1.0F, 0.0F, NULL; calls ftAnim_8006EBA4; and assigns fn_801090D4 to accessory4_cb. It neither removes an old item before overwriting xC0 nor resets xC4/xC8. ftKb_SpecialNIc_80108E14 performs the same transient resets for ftKb_MS_PpSpecialAirN. Its exact guard is (s32)xC4 == 0. That branch assigns specialn_pp_air_vertical_momentum to self_vel.y, sets xC4 true, and writes 0.0F to xC8. Otherwise self_vel.y is not directly changed and xC8 becomes -10.0F. This is a guarded assignment, not proof of positive upward velocity or a complete once-per-airtime invariant.\n\nBoth routines select ft_80459B88.hats[FTKIND_PEACH]->hat_dynamics[1], cast it to HSD_Joint*, pass it to ftCommon_SetAccessory, and pass the resulting accessory and the mapped FtPart_LThumbNb joint to lb_8000C2F8. The canonical PEACH index is explicit; resource appearance, aliasing, and why this copied-Popo path uses that index remain unresolved. No local null/bounds checks protect these object, attribute, hat, dynamics, accessory, part, or joint accesses. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L53-L102.\n\n## Command-driven item lifecycle\nfn_801090D4 has internal linkage through its preceding static declaration. It reads cmd_vars[0] into a u32. Command zero returns immediately. Command one samples parts[0].joint through lb_8000B1CC, adds specialn_pp_x_spawn * facing_dir to X and specialn_pp_y_spawn + xC8 to Y, then passes the vector, fighter object, It_Kind_Kirby_IceClimberIce, and facing direction to it_802C1590. The nullable constructor result overwrites xC0. The creation sound 0x1FBE5 is played whether construction succeeds or fails. Only a non-null result installs ftKb_Init_800EE74C in death2_cb and ftKb_Init_800EE7B8 in take_dmg_cb. Command one is consumed on either outcome. There is no guard against replacing an already tracked item.\n\nCommand two acts only when xC0 is non-null: it calls it_802C16F8, clears the command, invokes ft_800881D8 with 0x2233B and ft_PlaySFX with 0x1FBE8, and performs conditional current-field reference clearing. With no item, command two remains pending. All other u32 values remain unchanged and have no local operation. Neither release nor failed construction explicitly clears the death/damage callback fields, and this TU does not explicitly uninstall accessory4_cb. Producer timing, engine dispatch order, uninstallation, and complete callback lifetime remain unresolved. One tracking slot is not a proof of one globally live projectile. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L28-L28 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L171-L209.\n\nThe actual constructor copies the supplied vector into SpawnItem.prev_pos and forces its Z to zero, while obtaining SpawnItem.pos separately from the parent. It initializes velocity to zero and retains the owner for later notification. Thus the computed vector is a constructor input, not proof that every item position field initially equals it. The release helper assigns facing-relative X velocity, zeros Y/Z velocity, sets its release flag, and calls the helper entering item state 2. Removal forwards to Item_8026A8EC. The destruction callback, if its retained owner is non-null, routes the native ice kind to Popo and the alternate kind to Kirby's explicit-item notification helper, then clears its retained owner. Complete generic destruction scheduling and owner lifetime are not proved by this immediate chain. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/it/kinds/itclimbersice.c#L87-L156 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/it/kinds/itclimbersice.c#L252-L262.\n\n## Ownership and reference clearing\nftKb_SpecialNIc_80108CE8 compares the explicit Item_GObj* argument with the currently stored xC0 and stores NULL only on equality. A different item is ignored. NULL against NULL performs a redundant NULL store. It does not itself destroy the item. This helper genuinely protects a different currently tracked item from a stale non-null notification.\n\nftKb_SpecialNIc_80108D04 returns without removal for a null tracked pointer. Otherwise it requests removal, reacquires fighter user data, and compares fp->u.kb.xC0 with fp2->u.kb.xC0. Both are post-call field reads; the original item pointer was not saved. With unchanged fighter user data, these expressions refer to the same field. The collision handlers and command-two release use the same pattern. These comparisons therefore do not generally protect a replacement item installed during a callee. The distinction is structural and does not require guessing callback behavior. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L30-L51, code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L132-L169, and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L195-L207.\n\n## Motion callbacks and boundaries\nBoth Anim callbacks have a sole local guard: !ftAnim_IsFramesRemaining(gobj). On that result the ground callback calls ft_8008A2BC and the aerial callback calls ftCo_Fall_Enter. While the predicate is true they perform no local transition. They do not explicitly clean up tracked items. Both IASA bodies are empty, establishing no callback-local cancellation, not engine-wide uninterruptibility. Ground Phys unconditionally delegates to ft_80084F3C; air Phys delegates to ft_80084EEC. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/kinds/ftKirby/ftkirbyspecialiceclimber.c#L104-L130.\n\nThe ground physics helper applies common ground friction and ground movement, multiplying friction only when ABS(gr_vel) > walk_max_vel. Equality does not take this branch; an unordered NaN comparison does not satisfy the ordered greater-than test. The air helper forwards gravity and terminal_velocity to ftCommon_Fall and aerial_friction to ftCommon_ApplyFrictionAir. These calls alone do not prove unconditional descent, finite velocity, or a terminal bound for every exceptional input. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ft_084E.c#L33-L53.\n\nGround Coll branches on !ft_80082708(gobj). Inside that branch it optionally removes a non-null tracked item and performs current-field clearing, then always calls ftCo_Fall_Enter regardless of item presence. Air Coll branches exactly on ft_80081D0C(gobj) != GA_Ground. It optionally removes the item, resets xC4/xC8, and calls ftCo_LandingFallSpecial_Enter(gobj, false, specialn_pp_landing_lag). The comma expression in its pointer comparison contributes only its second operand. A GA_Ground result causes no move-specific reset.
